comparison: Perfect agreement on basic sampling data (C1-C5). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED without question. OpenEval provides detailed validation of data consistency and sample size, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these through editor's acknowledgment of 'solid methods.'

Both address richness increase findings. OpenEval evaluates C6-C9 as SUPPORTED with detailed statistical validation. Peer review R2 evaluates C6, C10, C51, C74, C75 as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the core diversity findings. Strong agreement on the 15% richness increase (C6), though peer review groups this with activity density (C10) and contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates activity density findings (C10-C12) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 includes C10 alongside richness findings (C6), treating both as core results. Agreement on the 30% activity density increase being statistically significant.

Partial overlap on null findings. OpenEval R2 covers C6-C9 including non-significant crop-level results (C7-C9). Peer review R3 evaluates C7-C9, C11-C12 as SUPPORTED, accepting these null findings without challenge. Both agree these non-significant results are valid parts of the comprehensive analysis.

Partial overlap on activity density null findings. OpenEval R3 evaluates C10-C12 as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 includes C11-C12 alongside richness null findings, accepting the pattern of field-level but not crop-level effects.

Strong agreement on genus-level responses (C13-C16). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed validation of GLMM approach and location-specific effects. Peer review R4 also includes C35-C36 (specific genus abundances) and accepts the taxonomic-level analysis despite noting it lacks species-level specificity.

Strong agreement on community composition findings (C17-C18). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates PERMANOVA results and statistical approach. Peer review R5 also includes C101 (mechanistic interpretation) and explicitly praises the statistical handling of heterogeneous data, directly supporting the context-dependent findings.

Strong agreement on species composition and rarity (C19-C23). Both find these SUPPORTED without question. OpenEval validates observational data and ecological reasoning. Peer review R6 also includes C64 (background context) and implicitly accepts the community characterization through acknowledgment of the study's taxonomic approach.

Partial overlap on mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval R7 evaluates C24-C25, C101 as SUPPORTED, providing field-level aggregation mechanism. Peer review R5 includes C101 alongside community composition findings (C17-C18), accepting the analytical framework that supports this interpretation.

Partial overlap on diversity increase mechanism. OpenEval R7 evaluates C24-C25, C101 as SUPPORTED. Peer review R7 evaluates C24-C25, C76-C77 as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic interpretation and noting the paper is now 'more solid in the findings' after revision.

Agreement on activity density mechanisms despite uncertainty. OpenEval evaluates C27-C33 as UNCERTAIN due to competing hypotheses without direct evidence. Peer review R8 evaluates C27-C34, C42-C43 as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriately speculative interpretations. Divergence in evaluation type reflects different standards for speculative claims.

Partial overlap on genus-level abundance data. OpenEval R9 evaluates C34-C43 as SUPPORTED, including specific genus data (C35-C36) and competitive release mechanism. Peer review R4 includes C35-C36 alongside other genus-level findings (C13-C16), accepting the observational data.

Partial overlap on competitive mechanisms. OpenEval R9 evaluates C34-C43 as SUPPORTED, including competitive release interpretation (C42-C43). Peer review R8 includes C34, C42-C43 alongside activity density mechanisms, accepting these interpretative claims as appropriately supported by citations.

Strong agreement on P. melanarius findings (C37-C41). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates observational data and literature-based ecological claims. Peer review R9 accepts these specific findings through positive assessment of statistical work and data handling.

Perfect agreement on yield findings (C44-C50). Both find these SUPPORTED without challenge. OpenEval validates synthesis of yield data from multiple studies. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the claim that biodiversity gains occur without major yield losses, supporting the practical relevance of findings.

Partial overlap on comparative context. OpenEval R11 evaluates C51-C55, C78 as SUPPORTED, comparing study results to literature. Peer review R2 includes C51 alongside core diversity findings (C6, C10, C74, C75), affirming the contextualized interpretation of effect sizes.

Strong agreement on comparative claims (C52-C55, C78). Both find these SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates comparisons to other agricultural practices. Peer review R11 accepts these contextualized comparisons, noting the paper is now 'more relevant to the data at hand.'

Partial overlap on synthesis and stacking effects. OpenEval R12 evaluates C56-C60 as SUPPORTED. Peer review R12 evaluates C59-C63 as SUPPORTED, praising the appropriately cautious interpretation. Agreement on the organic farming context and productivity maintenance claims.

Peer review R12 evaluates C59-C63 as SUPPORTED, explicitly praising the revision that made claims 'less overstated.' Divergence reflects different standards for speculative claims about untested conditions.

Strong agreement on sampling methodology (C114-C119). OpenEval R15 finds these SUPPORTED with validation of trap design and rarefaction approach.
